api_analysis.hypothesis: The illegal memory access is caused by passing host pointers (shape_vec.data(), strides_vec.data()) to the CUDA kernel, which dereferences them on device as device pointers. The kernel then reads invalid device addresses, leading to cudaErrorIllegalAddress.
evidence: custom_ops.cu hardtanh_launcher accepts const int64_t* shape and const int64_t* strides, and hardtanh_kernel dereferences them on device.
custom_ops_binding.cpp allocates std::vector<int64_t> shape_vec and strides_vec on host, then passes shape_vec.data() and strides_vec.data() to the launcher.
CUDA kernels cannot dereference host memory; passing host pointers to device code causes illegal memory access.
Input is contiguous (stride [12582912, 4194304, 2048, 1]), so stride-based indexing is unnecessary; a simple linear index is sufficient.
changes: Replace hardtanh_kernel in kernels/custom_ops.cu with a contiguous 1D kernel that uses output[i] and input[i], eliminating shape/strides device dereferences.
Remove NDIM template, shape, and strides parameters from the kernel and launcher; pass only output, input, numel, min_val, max_val, stream.
Update kernels/custom_ops_binding.cpp to call the simplified launcher without constructing shape/strides host vectors.
Keep model_new.py unchanged as it already calls cuda_extension.hardtanh_forward(x).
Expected result: kernel runs without illegal memory access and correctly clamps values to [-1,1].
